linkedin:
A QR code doesn't have to look like a scrap of static on a package. QRON runs the code through an image-generation pipeline so it renders as real artwork on the label, poster, or card — while staying fully scannable. Under the artwork, each code is Ed25519-signed and anchored under the AuthiChain protocol, so a scan can verify the code's authenticity instead of just trusting whatever URL happens to be embedded.

The art isn't just decoration — the same code carries a "Living Portal": the destination behind it can be updated after the code is already printed, so a changed link doesn't force a reprint.

If the QR codes on your packaging today are plain black-and-white grids nobody looks at twice, take a look at what a signed, art-rendered code can do instead.

https://qron.space/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=qron-signed-art&utm_content=b

reddit.title: We turn QR codes into actual artwork instead of a black-and-white grid — still fully scannable
reddit.body:
QRON runs each QR code through an image-generation pipeline, so what ends up on a label, poster, or card is real artwork instead of the standard black-and-white grid — while staying scannable by any reader. Under the art, each code is Ed25519-signed and anchored under the AuthiChain protocol, so a scan verifies the code's authenticity instead of trusting whatever URL happens to be embedded.

The same code also carries a "Living Portal": the destination behind it can be updated after the code is printed, so a changed link doesn't force a reprint.

Curious whether an art-rendered QR code actually gets more people to scan it in your experience, or whether that wears off as a novelty.

Disclosure: I work on this project.
